title: Generating Structured Outputs from Language Models: Benchmark and Studies
evidence_note: Full text. Benchmarks six engines (Guidance, Outlines, llama.cpp, XGrammar, OpenAI, Gemini) on real JSON Schemas under greedy decoding. Its contribution is coverage as a first-class metric: engines differ by 2x in how many schemas they accept at all, and an unsupported schema surfaces as a compile error or runtime failure rather than a wrong output. Reports grammar compilation time, TTFT and TPOT separately; finds constrained decoding can be ~50% faster than unconstrained and improves downstream task quality by up to 4%.

title: Fast Controlled Generation from Language Models with Adaptive Weighted Rejection Sampling
evidence_note: Metadata and abstract checked; theorem assumptions and domain-specific measurements require full-text coding.

title: The Hidden Cost of Structure: How Constrained Decoding Affects Language Model Performance
evidence_note: Metadata and abstract checked; model/task strata and log-probability analysis require full-text coding.

title: Thinking Before Constraining: A Unified Decoding Framework for Large Language Models
evidence_note: Full text. Decouples P(R|q) from P(A|R,q,F) so reasoning runs unconstrained and the FSM only engages after a trigger token, making constrained decoding a parser over the finished reasoning trace rather than a constraint on it. Same interleaving idea as CRANE but triggered lexically and in a single call. Reports 100% parse rate, up to 27% accuracy gain over natural generation, 5-20 extra tokens, and identifies premature trigger firing as the main failure mode across 1.5B-32B models.

title: Draft-Conditioned Constrained Decoding for Structured Generation in LLMs
evidence_note: Full text. Identifies feasible mass - the model probability remaining after masking - as the quantity that governs distortion, and formalises the projection tax as the expected log of its reciprocal. Rather than correcting the mask, it raises feasible mass beforehand by conditioning generation on an unconstrained draft, then masks as usual, so validity is still exact. K drafts are scored by cumulative log feasible mass. Reports 39.04% vs 15.24% strict structured accuracy on GSM8K at 1B scale.

title: We Need Structured Output: Towards User-centered Constraints on Large Language Model Output
evidence_note: Metadata and abstract checked; user study reports 134 use cases from 51 industry professionals.

title: XGrammar: Flexible and Efficient Structured Generation Engine for Large Language Models
evidence_note: Full text screened for the grammar compiler, persistent-stack execution, adaptive token masks, and serving evaluation; detailed evidence-level coding remains.

title: SynCode: LLM Generation with Grammar Augmentation
evidence_note: arXiv metadata and abstract checked; soundness assumptions, grammar coverage, and tokenizer integration require full-text coding.

title: IterGen: Iterative Semantic-aware Structured LLM Generation with Backtracking
evidence_note: Metadata and abstract only. Maintains a symbol-to-position map over the grammar so generation can move backward as well as forward, regenerating a grammar symbol in place using cached key-value state. Reported on privacy leakage and on SQL / Vega-Lite accuracy. Full-text coding still needed for guarantees and systems measurements.

title: FANTAstic SEquences and Where to Find Them: Faithful and Efficient API Call Generation through State-tracked Constrained Decoding and Reranking
evidence_note: Full text. API documentation is compiled into a constrained token search trie; structural tokens (dot, parenthesis, equals, comma) act as field boundaries that trigger constraint retrieval, so enforcement is per token within a per-field state machine. Faithfulness to the documentation holds by construction rather than by proof. A RoBERTa discriminator reranks beam candidates. Reports 1.56-2.39x speed-up over unconstrained beam search and prompt savings from dropping API docs from context.

title: Let Me Speak Freely? A Study on the Impact of Format Restrictions on Performance of Large Language Models
evidence_note: Full text. A study, not a method: compares decode-level JSON mode against prompt-level format-restricting instructions and a two-stage natural-language-then-convert pipeline. The result splits by task type - decode-level restriction is significantly worse on reasoning (GSM8K, Last Letter) but competitive or better on classification (DDXPlus, Sports). Stricter schemas also raise prompt sensitivity. Schema-guaranteed generation still degrades reasoning relative to free-form, which is the finding the later Constraint Tax and CRANE work builds on. Token cost by format is in the appendix; YAML is cheapest.

title: Automata-based constraints for language model decoding
evidence_note: Full text. Treats detokenization itself as a finite-state transducer and composes it with the constraint automaton, which is what makes tokenization misalignment disappear rather than be patched around; tokens may straddle grammar-rule boundaries. Coverage is deliberately bounded to regular languages and deterministic context-free languages (LL(k), LR(k)), not arbitrary or ambiguous CFGs. Correctness proofs in Appendix B. Reports roughly 7,000x faster compilation and 6.5-33.6x lower per-step cost than Outlines.

title: Sketch-Guided Constrained Decoding for Boosting Blackbox Large Language Models without Logit Access
evidence_note: arXiv metadata and abstract checked; black-box sketch protocol and final guarantee boundary require full-text coding.

title: Grammar-Aligned Decoding
evidence_note: Full text. Diagnoses standard grammar-constrained decoding as a binary approximation that assigns weight one to every grammatical prefix, which distorts the grammar-conditioned distribution. ASAp instead estimates expected future grammaticality and back-propagates it from completed samples, so the correction is iterative rather than single-pass. Theorem 1 gives an upper-bound property and Theorem 2 convergence to exact conditional sampling as iterations grow. Reports KL to the base model, not just validity.

title: SGLang: Efficient Execution of Structured Language Model Programs
evidence_note: arXiv metadata and abstract checked; structured-generation backend is one component of a broader language-model programming and serving system.

title: GRAMMAR-LLM: Grammar-Constrained Natural Language Generation

title: Flexible and Efficient Grammar-Constrained Decoding
evidence_note: Full text. Precomputes a token spanner table mapping terminal sequences to vocabulary tokens from the terminal regexes, a lexing automaton and the tokenizer, which moves the cost off the online path without per-grammar offline blowup. Notes that existing implementations contain soundness bugs, so the contribution is partly correctness rather than speed. Reports 17.71x faster offline preprocessing and 5-32ms per-token masking; no downstream generation-quality numbers are given.

title: CRANE: Reasoning with constrained LLM generation
evidence_note: Full text. Argues constraints cost reasoning capacity, not just accuracy: Proposition 3.1 shows constant-layer LLMs under restrictive grammars are limited to TC0. The remedy is an augmented grammar Ga -> R G that reserves an unconstrained reasoning region R before the constrained answer G, with delimiters toggling masking on and off mid-generation. Proposition 3.3 shows the augmented form preserves Turing-complete simulation while keeping the extracted answer in L(G). Up to 10 points on GSM-Symbolic and FOLIO, verified with Z3 and Prover9.

title: Syntactic and Semantic Control of Large Language Models via Sequential Monte Carlo
evidence_note: Full text. Constraints are arbitrary non-negative potentials; cheap ones act as token-level proposals, expensive ones as twist functions applied at reweighting. Particles are extended, reweighted and resampled, so rejection is a population-level reallocation rather than a per-token mask. Convergence to the global product of experts is asymptotic in particle count and assumes potential monotonicity. Reports task accuracy plus KL divergence to the target distribution, and 5-10x particle savings over sample-rerank.

title: Efficient and Asymptotically Unbiased Constrained Decoding for Large Language Models
evidence_note: Full text. Theorem 2.1 lower-bounds the bias that ordinary constrained decoding introduces, so the distortion is not an implementation artefact. DISC replaces masking with importance sampling plus acceptance-rejection over a lexicographically sorted constraint matrix, giving an unbiased draw from the constrained distribution; Theorem 3.1 shows KL to the true constrained distribution vanishes exponentially in the retry budget, with expected retries bounded independently of it. Parallel prefix verification is O(log N) per candidate and 8.5x faster than trie baselines.

title: Earley-Driven Dynamic Pruning for Efficient Structured Decoding
evidence_note: Full text. Prunes Earley items that cannot contribute to any completion using a dependency graph over Predict/Scan/Complete edges, plus a rejected-prefix set that lets the parser discard all extensions of a byte sequence once it is known dead. Correctness is argued from reachability rather than proved equivalent to unpruned masking, which is worth noting given the claimed 2x speedup. Reports throughput up to 12,174 tok/s against 616 for XGrammar on one workload, and an ablation showing pruning is worth 30-50%.

title: XGrammar-2: Efficient Dynamic Structured Generation Engine for Agentic LLMs
evidence_note: Full text screened for dynamic grammar fragments, cross-grammar reuse, agentic tool formats, JIT compilation, and serving measurements.

title: Accelerating Constrained Decoding with Token Space Compression
evidence_note: Full text. Compresses the vocabulary into equivalence classes that are interchangeable for prefix validity under a Greibach-normal-form PDA, so the mask is computed over class representatives instead of all tokens. Theorem 1 makes the compression provably lossless: outputs are byte-identical to uncompressed masking, so this is a pure cost reduction with no behavioural change. Reports 318-478s offline precomputation, 253-3095 equivalence classes, and up to 7.5x speedup on complex grammars.

title: Future Validity is the Missing Statistic: From Impossibility to Phi-Estimation for Grammar-Faithful Speculative Decoding
evidence_note: Full text. Formalises the gap between locally projected masking and the true grammar-conditional distribution as a missing future-validity factor, recovered by a Doob h-transform. Offers a four-tier estimator ladder from uniform (status quo, free) through one-step lookahead and Monte Carlo rollouts to exact dynamic programming. Theorem 7 bounds total variation by the estimator error; exact computation is #P-complete for general CFGs. Measures TV directly: 0.418 under uniform versus 0.014 under the exact oracle on Dyck, and reports structural bias (local projection overproduces nesting depth and length).

title: AdapTrack: Constrained Decoding without Distorting LLM's Output Intent
evidence_note: Full text. Keeps a validity estimate per prefix and, once masking reveals that a chosen branch has lost probability mass, backtracks by rejection sampling and resamples excluding the dead branch. Theorem 5.1 preserves relative probabilities among valid sequences. Figure 1 is the canonical illustration of constraint-induced substitution: the model wants torch.matrix_rank (57.44%), the constraint removes it as absent from the target library version, and renormalisation elects torch.matrix_power (originally 0.20%) rather than the nearby valid torch.linalg.matrix_rank. Costs 20-60% more model calls.

title: ChopChop: a Programmable Framework for Semantically Constraining the Output of Language Models
evidence_note: Full text. Constrains abstract syntax trees rather than token strings, using regular codata (cyclic term graphs) to represent infinite program spaces finitely, with Brzozowski-derivative parser coterms and e-graphs for the equivalence case study. Decoding keeps a worklist of prefixes and discards any prefix that cannot be completed to satisfy the predicate, so the mechanism is completability lookahead with backtracking rather than a precomputed mask. Theorem 3.3 gives soundness conditional on a sound pruner; Theorem 3.4 gives relative completeness under top-p/top-k. Type safety is handled by overapproximation.

title: The Constraint Tax: Measuring Validity-Correctness Tradeoffs in Structured Outputs for Small Language Models
evidence_note: Full text screened for schema-valid versus executable-correct outcomes, delayed packaging, model-size scope, and constrain-late recommendation.

title: Decode-Time Grammars: Constrained LLM Generation over a Refinement Order of Grammar Fragments
evidence_note: Full text. Grammar fragments are indexed by an environment scope Gamma (in-scope names, sorts, schema entries, API members, tool state) and projected into typed slots at reference positions; enforcement is a token mask over a CFG recogniser, applied hole by hole across a sketch stage and a constrained-realisation stage. Theorem 1 gives no-ghost soundness conditional on the masking engine being an exact incremental recogniser; Proposition 3 shows no static masking family is both sound and non-blocking over an unbounded name space. Reports 10.6-17.8% throughput reduction versus XGrammar and SQL execution match rising from 76% to 100%.

evidence_note: Official PLDI metadata and abstract checked; the work formalizes prefix automata and inhabitable-type search for well-typed generation.

title: Syntactic Control of Language Models by Posterior Inference
evidence_note: ACL Anthology metadata and abstract checked; posterior inference combines SMC with a syntactic tagger for target constituency structure.

title: Efficient Guided Generation for Large Language Models
evidence_note: Full text. Reformulates regex- and CFG-guided generation as iterative FSM/PDA processing, pre-indexing vocabulary transitions so valid-token retrieval is O(1) on average rather than scanning the vocabulary. The Outlines implementation masks invalid next tokens and guarantees generated structure under the supported grammar assumptions. Reports construction time, per-token overhead, and an approximately 50 MB naively built Python-grammar index.

title: Don't Fine-Tune, Decode: Syntax Error-Free Tool Use via Constrained Decoding
evidence_note: Full text. Compiles tool syntax into an FSM, maps valid character transitions to model tokens, and masks invalid next tokens during inference. Across ToolEval and FuncQA it eliminates syntax errors and measures downstream tool-use accuracy; the paper also reports negligible additional compute and memory overhead relative to model inference. The guarantee is syntactic membership, not correct tool or argument selection.

title: COLLIE: Systematic Construction of Constrained Text Generation Tasks
evidence_note: Full text and archival OpenReview record. Defines a grammar for compositional count and position constraints across character, word, sentence, paragraph, and passage levels; compiles 13 constraint structures into COLLIE-v1 and evaluates completed generations with executable checks. It is a benchmark and constraint-construction framework, not a token-time enforcement method, so allocation is framework-dependent and no decoding guarantee is assigned.

title: Constrained Decoding for Fill-in-the-Middle Code Language Models via Efficient Left and Right Quotienting of Context-Sensitive Grammars
evidence_note: Full text. Extends Earley parsing with left and right language quotients so fill-in-the-middle code is checked against both contexts, including practical handling of lexing and Python indentation. Greedy decoding rejects candidates that cannot connect to the suffix and evaluates 95,390 examples in each of two Python FIM datasets. No blanket language-soundness label is assigned because the documented whitespace-sensitive implementation deliberately accepts a completeness–soundness tradeoff and can admit some invalid programs.

title: NeuroLogic A*esque Decoding: Constrained Text Generation with Lookahead Heuristics
evidence_note: Full text. Adds A*-inspired future-cost estimates to NeuroLogic's beam search so partial hypotheses are ranked by both model score and predicted future constraint satisfaction. Evaluates five tasks including CommonGen, table-to-text, constrained translation, and question generation. The method improves empirical constraint satisfaction and task metrics but does not state a hard satisfaction or distributional guarantee.

title: Logically Constrained Decoding
evidence_note: Full text. A symbolic engine updates an explicit world model while decoding and permits only prefixes of legal chess moves or sound propositional-resolution steps. The construction supplies semantic/state validity for the checked step under the chess or proof oracle, while experiments measure legal-play/proof outcomes across several model families and report token-throughput overhead. It does not claim general mathematical correctness beyond the two implemented world models.

title: Constrained Decoding with Speculative Lookaheads
evidence_note: Full text. Uses a smaller draft model to speculate lookahead continuations, validates them with the target model and task reward, and accepts or rejects speculative paths inside constrained beam search. Evaluates sentiment, harmlessness, toxicity, and lexical-control tasks while reporting inference speedup and reward/constraint performance. The speed–quality method is empirical and does not provide a hard constraint-satisfaction guarantee.

title: Constrained Decoding of Diffusion LLMs with Context-Free Grammars
evidence_note: Full text. Reduces diffusion and multi-region infilling feasibility to emptiness of the intersection between a CFG and a regular language, then uses that decision procedure to retain exactly token assignments that admit a valid completion. Evaluates C++ infilling, JSON, and diffusion-language-model generation, reporting syntactic and functional correctness plus practical overhead. The guarantee concerns membership/reachability in the formal language, not application semantics.

title: DINGO: Constrained Inference for Diffusion LLMs
evidence_note: Full text and NeurIPS record. Uses dynamic programming over regex-automaton states and a diffusion model's per-position distributions to choose the highest-probability valid token block. Proposition 4.1 proves a valid-prefix property and Proposition 4.2 proves per-block optimality under the stated factorized output distribution. Evaluates symbolic math and JSON and reports runtime; the paper explicitly limits optimality in semi-autoregressive multi-block settings.

title: Constrained Discrete Diffusion
evidence_note: Full text. Projects intermediate categorical diffusion distributions toward differentiable feasible sets, with augmented-Lagrangian variants for multiple constraints. Theorem 4.1 gives a non-asymptotic bound on KL distance to a prox-regular feasible set rather than exact task-level correctness; experiments report zero observed violations for toxicity, molecular properties, and lexical instructions plus runtime overhead. Accordingly, empirical adherence is recorded as an outcome, not upgraded to semantic correctness.

title: Mitigating Bias in Locally Constrained Decoding via Tractable Proposals
evidence_note: Full text. Tensorizes finite automata on GPU to build globally constrained proposals that retain only prefixes completable within a fixed horizon, then circuit-multiplies the automaton with an HMM approximation to form probabilistic proposals and potentials for SMC. The fixed-horizon construction guarantees constraint satisfaction at termination, while the SMC estimator targets the model distribution conditioned on the constraint asymptotically. Evaluates function calling, CommonGen, and Spider with accuracy, satisfaction, convergence, latency, and memory measurements.

title: Lost in Space: Finding the Right Tokens for Structured Output
evidence_note: Full text and ACL Anthology record. Uses llama.cpp's unmodified GBNF token masking to compare five semantically similar output formats across eight models and four NLP benchmarks. Finds that token choice, especially leading whitespace, changes downstream predictions and can improve performance by 5–10%. This is a measurement of grammar–tokenization interaction; it does not introduce a new enforcement algorithm.

title: StructEval: Benchmarking LLMs' Capabilities to Generate Structural Outputs
evidence_note: Full text and TMLR record. Benchmarks generation and conversion for 18 renderable and non-renderable formats across 44 task types, using format-specific parsers, key validation, and rendered-output assessment. It evaluates structural fidelity of completed outputs rather than enforcing constraints during generation, so no masking behavior or language guarantee is inferred.
